claims.text: In a UK Biobank cohort aged 37-73 years, 3% of participants (16,538 / 493,737) were classified as frail.
In a UK Biobank cohort aged 37-73 years, 38% of participants (185,360 / 493,737) were classified as pre-frail.
In a UK Biobank cohort aged 37-73 years, 59% of participants (291,839 / 493,737) were classified as not frail.
Frailty is significantly associated with multimorbidity, with an odds ratio of 27.1 for individuals with four or more long-term conditions.
Multiple sclerosis is the long-term condition most strongly associated with frailty (OR 15.3, 99.75% CI 12.8-18.2).
Chronic fatigue syndrome is significantly associated with frailty (OR 12.9, 99.75% CI 11.1-15.0).
Pre-frailty and frailty are significantly associated with all-cause mortality across all age strata in men and women, except in women aged 37-45 years.

evidence.description: 493 737 participants aged 37-73 years were included in the study, of whom 16 538 (3%) were considered frail
Frailty was significantly associated with multimorbidity (prevalence 18% [4435/25 338] in those with four or more long-term conditions; odds ratio [OR] 27·1, 95% CI 25·3-29·1)
The top five long-term conditions associated with frailty were multiple sclerosis (OR 15·3; 99·75% CI 12·8-18·2)
Pre-frailty and frailty were significantly associated with mortality for all age strata in men and women (except in women aged 37-45 years) after adjustment for confounders.

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort analysis using multinomial logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards modeling
methodologies.description: Frailty phenotype based on five Fried criteria was evaluated against multimorbidity, specific conditions, and all-cause mortality over a median 7-year follow-up.
conditions: Stratified by age (37-45, 45-55, 55-65, 65-73 years) and sex
Adjusted for multimorbidity count, socioeconomic status, BMI, smoking status, and alcohol use

limitations.text: Little was known about the prevalence or effects of frailty on mortality in younger populations prior to this study.
Pre-frailty and frailty were not significantly associated with mortality in women aged 37-45 years after adjustment for confounders.

future_work.text: Research, clinical guidelines, and healthcare services must shift focus from single conditions to the requirements of complex patient populations with multimorbidity and frailty.
